<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s).

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface OpenAuthoringWriter))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), getMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in createOpenAuthoringRegistry), getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol), saveMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in createOpenAuthoringRegistry))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in createOpenAuthoringRegistry), getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), saveMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface OpenAuthoringWriter))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via deleteMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol), getMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in createOpenAuthoringRegistry), getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol), getMetaTypes (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol), saveMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface OpenAuthoringWriter))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (literal, a string literal in OpenAuthoringProtocol; a string literal in REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface OpenAuthoringWriter))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via openWriter (symbol, a top-level function), delete_metadata_draft (literal, a string literal in OPEN_AUTHORING_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES; a string literal in WRITE_TOOLS; a string literal in createOpenAuthoringRegistry), save_metadata_draft (literal, a string literal in OPEN_AUTHORING_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES; a string literal in WRITE_TOOLS; a string literal in createOpenAuthoringRegistry))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9b6b14649149d36f09dab245c0962f00ff109e1f` — the merge of head `2d6a72269b60b270ca669ea19da843d0ec6b3ddf` into base `ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9b6b14649149d36f09dab245c0962f00ff109e1f && git checkout 9b6b14649149d36f09dab245c0962f00ff109e1f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36 2d6a72269b60b270ca669ea19da843d0ec6b3ddf && git checkout -B drift-repro ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36 && git merge --no-ff 2d6a72269b60b270ca669ea19da843d0ec6b3ddf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 full · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `8709c889fe206ee7e612fe3970fe86e87a30cf2c` · card #34766 (`Fixes #34766`, PR-b) · read 2026-11-18T10:13Z

Net diff against merge base `99a0e4fbfc`: 14 files, +1032 / -56. It adds the write half of the MCP draft door: two write tools, a publish verdict in the same reply, and verdicts on `list_drafts`.

### Against the card

- **`Fixes` is right.** PR-a (the read half) is merged. This PR carries the rest of the card's done-when, so the merge should close the card.
- **Done when, each item.**
  - A draft whose stored form fails a publish rule gets that finding in the save reply. The test runs the card's own example, the app-crm flow with no routable trigger.
  - The saved draft is a normal `mode: 'draft'` write, so it shows in Studio's Changes review. The reply links both the Changes view and the item review.
  - A caller the D1 gate does not admit sees none of the five tools. That gate is on main and unchanged here, and the `initialize` drafts line is served only when the tools are.
- **File surface.** The card says the PR reads `packages/metadata-protocol`, but it changes protocol source: `draftPublishJudgement` becomes public and can read the stored draft itself. Claim 6974854210 names this PR's 14 files at this head, so the change is inside the claimed surface. I note the gap between card and claim for the seat.

### Read at the head

- **Gate order on the write doors, at rule level.**
  - The type name is folded through the one canonical helper on every path, so an alias cannot pass a gate under one spelling and be written under another.
  - Save and discard each run the type-level write admission for their own verb, then the walled-catalog verdict, then the write. A refusal at any step writes nothing.
  - Save needs a package. A missing one is a 400 that names the packages the caller can write, capped. Writability itself stays with the repository.
  - There is no publish tool and no force flag. Every save is `mode: 'draft'` on the MCP surface with the client recorded, and `ifMatch` maps to the parent version.
- **Verdicts are gated, at rule level.**
  - The save reply runs the type-level read admission before any verdict. When it refuses, the draft is still saved and the reply carries `verdict: null` with the refusal in `verdictWithheld`.
  - `list_drafts` runs the type-level read admission, then the item read gate under the stored-version door policy, then the judgement. A withheld or failed verdict is `null`, never a partial one.
  - A judgement that throws becomes `verdictError`, not a failed save.
- **`draftPublishJudgement`.** It is public now and takes an optional body. With no body it reads the stored draft for that package (and member, when one is given), and a missing draft is a 404 `NO_DRAFT`. Callers that pass a body behave as before.
- **Wiring rows.** `REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS` has the new producer (by face, always draft). The durability gate has the new failure-propagation site. `system-context.mdx` row 55b and its register row name both doors and the writer. The skills surface guard checks all five tool names against the native tools, and I found no hosted tool with the same name.
- **Tests.** There are 36 runtime cases. They cover the save verdict, the fold, a write-admission refusal, a withheld verdict, a walled save and a walled discard, a verdict error, no writer, the item gate on `list_drafts`, the card's app-crm case, a schema refusal relaying `issues[]`, and an inherited member name. There are also the protocol cases for the body-less read and the 404, and the `initialize` cases for the drafts line.
- **Changesets, read sentence by sentence.** There are two: the runtime and MCP one, and the metadata-protocol one. Both are `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (new tools and a new public method, and no reply loses a key) and `Metadata-protocol: none` (what an author can write is unchanged). These are the right levels. No changeset already on main is edited.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `7d8dcf693a`.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 63 in total, all `success` or `skipped`. One `PR-body guards` run failed and was replaced by a green run on the same head.

### Should-check (for L2, does not block L1)

- The save reply runs only the type-level read admission before its verdict, while `list_drafts` also runs the item read gate. On save the caller just wrote the draft, so that difference looks right. L2 should still confirm that no finding in the verdict carries text from another item the caller could not read on its own.

### Nits (none blocks)

- A type value that is not a plain metadata type name can reach a 5xx instead of a 4xx. The dev report flags this out of scope with no carrier. It belongs in a small follow-up card.
- The write-tools changeset names an example and the admission it needs, in the same words as the read-half changeset already on main. The seat weighs this under the card's disclosure rule.
- The PR's assignee and its body's attribution lines do not follow the lane's usual shape. The seat can tidy these before landing.

### Not mine, still owed before landing

- **Contract review** at this head (the seat's run is in progress).
- Landing after that, through the seat.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8709c889fe206ee7e612fe3970fe86e87a30cf2c`
Local-runs: none

Full review of PR #35103 (PR-b of card #34766, the write half of the open draft door), declaration face. Read: the card body and all fourteen comments (the claims, the dev reports, and the PR-b hand-off 6968071928 among them); the PR body, its 14-file list, and the net diff against `main` (merge base `99a0e4fbfc`, +1032/-56); every PR comment, including L1-b's ACCEPT 6975500299; the four records on #35059 (6967316983, 6969515963, 6971674038, 6971726027); and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head to judge the diff's claims, and was not reviewed. There is no must-fix and one should-fix (S1, the cost of the per-draft verdicts, Prime Directive 5). The verdict is PASS.

Check-runs on the head, taking the latest run of each name: 55 names, 38 `success`, 17 `skipped`, none red and none in progress. All ten Test Core shards, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, every `Lint` run and the `PR-body guards` re-run at 09:46Z concluded `success`. The PR-body guard's 09:40Z red was the missing branch claim, and the re-run on the same head supersedes it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Only the write half is in the diff. RIGHT.**
   - None of the read half's four other files is in the diff: its changeset, the design note, `mcp.ts` and the route-envelope table.
   - For the three files with merge conflicts (the module, its test and the mcp surface guard), the net patch against the merge base is byte-identical to `78f3ab2aa3..7cbb4252a9`. That range is the write half's own delta on top of the landed read half. At the merge base, those files equal the landed squash `78f3ab2aa3`.
   - I checked this by reading git objects; nothing was run. No read-half hunk is re-added or reverted.
   - The hunks that touch read-tool code change nothing a read tool answers:
     - the item gate is factored into one local `itemGate`;
     - `typeReadRefusal` now goes through the shared `typeAdmission`, with the same predicate and the same caller;
     - two refusal texts are reworded.
   - The one exception is `list_drafts`, which now needs the verdict method (nit N3).
2. **(a) The folded type, through the one helper, with the human as the caller. RIGHT.**
   - The save and the discard each call `canonicalTypeOf(input.type)` once. The save hands that one value to the type-level write admission, the walled verdict, `saveMetaItem`, the type-level read admission, `draftPublishJudgement` and the review route. The discard hands it to the write admission, the walled verdict and `deleteMetaItem`.
   - `list_drafts` folds each row through the same helper before it asks any admission, gate or judgement.
   - The module defines the helper once, with no second copy.
   - The admissions read `readGate(...).resolveCaller()`. That is the caller built from the human's own grants, never the agent envelope's ceiling.
   - The walled verdict reads `posture` and `isSystem` off the request envelope, as every `/meta` write door and the MCP import door do. The envelope assembly takes `posture` from the human's own resolution for an agent principal and sets `isSystem: false`, so this is also the human's value.
   - The inherited-member fallback is unchanged from the read half (carried nit). On the real protocol it is refused and writes nothing; that is pinned.
3. **(b) The type-level write admission before anything is written, and refusal of a type the human may not write. RIGHT.**
   - The save asks `metaTypeWriteRefusal` as `PUT`, and the discard asks it as `DELETE`. Each does this before the walled verdict and before the protocol write, so a refusal writes nothing.
   - The verbs match the ones the `/meta` entry judges. `/meta`'s save path asks no other per-type write gate: after the type-level write admission come the authoring admission (D1 here), the walled verdict and the closed query set, and this door states no query.
   - A registry with no writer refuses both writes. A failed posture read answers 503 and writes nothing.
   - Pinned: both spellings are refused on both tools with no write call made, and a holder of the capability writes.
4. **(c) A verdict is told only where the type-level read admission admits the human. RIGHT.**
   - The save asks `metaTypeReadRefusal` after the save lands and before the judgement. If the human is refused, the reply carries `verdict: null` with `verdictWithheld`, and no judgement runs (pinned: the judgement is not called).
   - Each listed draft asks the same admission before any read of its body. Then come the strict draft read, the `/meta` item gate under `STORED_VERSION_DOOR_POLICY`, and the judgement.
   - A refusal or a fault at any step gives `null` plus the reason, never a partial verdict. For an unread type this is pinned: no protocol call names that type.
   - L1-b's should-check on the save, which runs no item gate: settled in ③ at rule level, with the detail in the reviewer's local note.
5. **(d) `list_drafts` stays at parity with the `/meta` drafts listing. RIGHT.**
   - The rows follow the `/meta` drafts listing's rule unchanged. Only the new `verdict` member is gated.
   - This PR does not widen into the listing's own admission.
6. **(e) No publish tool. RIGHT.**
   - The registry serves the three reads and the two writes, and nothing else. The `default` arm refuses any other name.
   - Every save is `mode: 'draft'`, `surface: 'mcp'`, with the write face of a door that has no `force`.
   - The request is built field by field, so nothing in `item` becomes a channel.
   - The discard is `state: 'draft'` only.
7. **(f) D4, the package requirement, and its named refusal. RIGHT.**
   - A save that names no package is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before any write. The refusal names up to 20 writable packages, taken from the protocol's own writability verdict, and it degrades to a pointer when they cannot be listed.
   - `package` is kept out of the schema's `required` list on purpose, so the named refusal can be reached. That is right.
   - Pinned on the fake protocol and on the real one: only a writable package is named, and nothing is written.
   - The discard takes `package` as optional. D4 names the save only.
8. **The public verdict method (D2). RIGHT.**
   - `draftPublishJudgement` is made public in place, with a facade delta of 0 lines.
   - With no `body`, it reads the stored draft at its address, including the member, and an empty address is refused `404 NO_DRAFT`, the strict draft read's own refusal. With a body, it behaves as before.
   - It is one judgement, not a second routine. The protocol pins check that its answer equals the body-handed call and that its refusals equal the per-item publish's 422 issues.
9. **Reply shapes and fail paths. RIGHT.**
   - A judgement that throws after the save landed is reported as `verdictError` beside the saved identity, never as a refused save. A coded refusal below 500 keeps its code; a fault is named without its text, and one warning is logged.
   - A coded protocol refusal now relays `issues[]`. That matches the `meta-dispatch` face, which trims the message to a headline. It is pinned on the real protocol with no write.
   - The `refusalFromThrown` declaration in `FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES` is the remedy that gate prescribes for a catch that returns the failure to its caller.
10. **Wiring and the drafts line. RIGHT.**
    - The `REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS` row (by face, always draft, so the body-only question) is right. So are the face note and row 55b of the system-context page with its generated register row.
    - The surface guard now checks all five names against the native tools.
    - The `initialize` paragraph is added only where `authoringToolsServed` holds, which is the same gate that registers the tools. A host's or the configured instructions still replace the default text whole. The paragraph's presence and absence are pinned.
11. **Done when. RIGHT.**
    - On a real protocol and a real SQL store, through the real domain, with the real identity door's envelope:
      - an unnamed save is refused with the writable package named;
      - the save answers the card's finding with its rule id, path and hint;
      - `list_drafts` lists the draft with an equal verdict;
      - the discard empties the list.
    - The second done-when cell, that a token without the authoring scope and an API key see no tool, is the D1 gate, which landed with the read half and is unchanged.
12. **Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract).**
    - **N1.** The D4 refusal, including its protocol read of the package list, comes before the type-level write admission. `/meta` asks that admission before it resolves the protocol. Nothing is disclosed, because the same human can list packages through the read tool. Moving the admission above D4 would mirror `/meta` exactly.
    - **N2.** The module header's read section still says `list_drafts` "runs no item gate". That is true of the rows, and the write section now gates each verdict. One clause would reconcile the two.
    - **N3.** `list_drafts` now answers 503 on a host whose protocol has no verdict method, where it used to list. Listing the rows with the verdict withheld would keep the read tool's old reach.
    - **N4.** The walled refusal is pinned for both writes. Its admit arm, the platform operator under a walled posture, is not pinned here. The predicate is the shared one.
    - Carried from the read half and unchanged: the inherited-member fallback answers 5xx rather than 4xx, the second gate-port builder, and a gate fault answering 500 rather than 503.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/34766-mcp-draft-door-write-tools.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` `patch` and `@objectstack/mcp` `patch`. RIGHT.
  - The runtime serves two new tools with new input schemas, and `list_drafts` gains a reply member.
  - `mcp` adds an `initialize` paragraph where the authoring tools are served.
  - No reply loses a member. The new exports of the module are not on the runtime's package entry.
- `.changeset/34766-mcp-draft-door-write.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch`. RIGHT. A private method of an exported class becomes public, and its `body` becomes optional, which widens what it accepts. The `REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS` row is a ledger row with no behaviour.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` in both changesets is RIGHT. The save runs the same `saveMetaItem`, schema and surface value that already exist, so nothing an author can write changes. A non-protocol widening ships `patch`, and no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- Every sentence of both changesets agrees with the code read in ①. No changeset already on `main` is edited. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.
- **Disclosure check: clean.** The changesets, the PR body, the commit messages unique to this branch and the new test names state rules. The one example they give, and the capability names they use, are words the landed read-half changeset already carries. None of them names a type the type-level admissions list, the capability such a type requires, or a field or returned content tied to those admissions.
- Clause-②: yes (widening). RIGHT in both changesets and in the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **L1-b should-check 6975500299 (verdict text and the item gate): settled.** The save's verdict and the listed verdicts meet the same read rules as the `/meta` draft read gives the same human for the same stored draft: no widening over `/meta`. A `/meta`-wide question it raised went to the seat privately (security-findings §6); it does not block this head.
- **S1 (should-fix) — Prime Directive 5: `list_drafts` computes its verdicts one draft at a time with no stated reason.**
  - Each listed draft costs a strict draft read, a second stored-row read inside the judgement, and a fresh listing of the package's drafts to build the publish closure.
  - So a package with N drafts makes about 3N reads and N closure collections over the same N rows, where one listing and one closure per package would serve them all.
  - The item gate's need for the strict read is a reason for that one read. It is not a reason for re-collecting the closure per draft, and the code states neither.
  - Fix: state the bound and the reason at the loop, or collect the package closure once and hand it to the judgement. Not blocking.
- **Hand-off 6968071928, every `left` item, answered.**
  - The local fold copy is gone (① item 2).
  - The durability site is declared (① item 9).
  - The final-head gates are answered by the check-runs.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is answered by `Build Core` and the type-check runs on the head.
  - The overlap with the expected neighbour is resolved: the dev's last report finds no conflicting head.
  - The WIP prefix is dropped, and the body says `Fixes #34766`.
- **Report 6967114632 `open_questions`.** Q1, wait or build on the old read head: superseded, because the read half is landed and merged in. Q2, the protocol-file neighbour: accepted as a clean neighbour, as the PR body records. Neither is open.
- **Report 6971531844: `security_findings: "withheld"`.** This concerned the write path's type-level admission. The rule it concerns is met at this head (① items 3 and 4). Nothing is left open on this PR.
